question: Why is indigotindisulfonate sodium short, and what do we do?

steps.title: Our stock in three hospitals
steps.purpose: Read on-hand stock and 28-day use where each hospital keeps it.

timeline.label: FDA posts the indigotindisulfonate sodium shortage

explanation.headline: FDA's records trace our supply to a plant classified VAI 64 days after the shortage posting

sentences.text: FDA's history shows an earlier shortage of indigotindisulfonate sodium first posted on 2022-08-23, since resolved, and the drug is not on FDA's current shortage list as of 2026-10-21.
The product label for NDC 81284031505 names CENEXI (FEI 3007250542) as the registered plant for analysis, manufacture, and pack.
FDA inspection 1245208 at that plant ended 2022-10-26 and was classified VAI — 64 days after FDA posted the shortage on 2022-08-23.
Earlier inspections at the same plant include an OAI classification in 2015 (inspection 924508) and VAI classifications in 2012, 2016, and 2018.
Corvale East holds 31 units at 4.4 per day for 7.1 days on hand; Corvale General holds 64 units at 4.3 per day for 14.8 days on hand.
The top-ranked option is to transfer 3 units of 8 mg/mL, 5 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East, which would leave Corvale General with 14 days and bring Corvale East to 8 days.

memory.text: Decision on cisplatin: transfer cisplatin between Corvale hospitals weekly instead of buying grey-market stock. Rationale: Grey-market offers were 6 to 10 times contract price with unverifiable pedigree (demo history). Approved by Jordan Hale, PharmD.

Decision on lidocaine: switch lidocaine 1% 30 mL vials to 5 mL vials in the ED to reduce waste during the shortage. Rationale: Single-dose waste was a third of use (demo history). Approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD.
